adviceContext.reasonsForAdvice: Planning for retirement, wanting to pay down debt faster, and ensuring adequate insurance coverage for our family.
adviceContext.currentSituation: Both working full-time with stable incomes. Have two children aged 12 and 15. Concerned about balancing mortgage repayments with retirement savings.
adviceContext.concerns: Worried about whether we're on track for retirement in 15-20 years. Also concerned about managing debt while maximizing super contributions.

advisorInput.analysis: The Smiths are in a strong financial position with combined income of $173,000 and total assets of $1.395M. Their debt-to-income ratio is manageable at approximately 2:1. Current superannuation balances are reasonable for their ages (50 and 47), but there's opportunity to increase contributions to maximize retirement outcomes.
advisorInput.recommendations: 1. Consider salary sacrificing additional amounts into super to reduce taxable income and boost retirement savings. 2. Implement a debt reduction strategy focusing on the higher-interest car loan first. 3. Review insurance coverage to ensure it aligns with current family needs and financial obligations. 4. Establish an emergency fund of 3-6 months expenses if not already in place.
advisorInput.strategies: Debt Snowball Strategy: Focus extra repayments on car loan to eliminate within 3 years. Super Boost Strategy: Increase combined super contributions by $10,000 annually through salary sacrifice. Insurance Optimization: Consolidate policies where possible to reduce premiums while maintaining adequate coverage. Investment Diversification: Consider adding property or international equities to investment portfolio for better diversification.
advisorInput.nextSteps: Schedule follow-up in 3 months to review implementation of salary sacrifice arrangements. Provide debt repayment calculator and projections. Arrange insurance policy review with specialist. Discuss estate planning and will updates.
